independent.summary: The item explicitly requires the billing.js fallback to become 'weekly', but GET /api/billing/:domain still returns `entity.leoRefreshFrequency ?? 'daily'`, so the billing API reports a daily cadence for any entity with no stored frequency (new entities now default to weekly) — the one named sub-task of the item that the diff never does.

The LeoRefresh checkout duplicate guard keys off `leoRefreshEnabled` alone, which was safe only while the webhook was the single writer; now a superadmin can flip the switch off on an entity that still has a live `leoRefreshSubscriptionId`, after which the owner sees the Enable button and can buy a second $10/mo add-on subscription (and conversely a comped entity gets 409 'already active' and can never actually subscribe, while cancel 400s for lack of a subscription id).

The item requires the webhook to never touch an entity with no `leoRefreshSubscriptionId`, but the `customer.subscription.deleted` addon branch still sets `leoRefreshEnabled = false` purely on `sub.metadata.domain` without comparing `sub.id` to the stored subscription id, so a Stripe redelivery or a stale/older add-on sub deletion silently revokes a superadmin comp.

The assertion commented 'An empty-string subscription id is no subscription' does not test that: `comped()` calls `entity(overrides)` and then deletes `leoRefreshSubscriptionId`, so the empty-string value is removed before `effectiveSchedule` sees it and the test only re-checks the absent-key case.

triageGrades.reason: The change adds leoRefreshEnabled to the superadminOnly list in dashboard.js and a `superadmin: true` rule in entitySettings.js, so authorization is genuinely touched.
No credentials, keys or env handling appear in the diff (the test's 'test-admin-key' is a stub header value, not a secret).
LeoRefresh is the $10/mo Stripe add-on and the diff changes who can enable it and hides the Stripe cancel path for comped entities, so the billing surface is touched.
Nothing is deleted or overwritten in bulk; only a boolean field and scheduling logic change.
The core of the change is a politeness cap on the outbound rescrape cadence in leoRefresh.js — it directly changes how often the crawler hits third-party sites — so external interaction is touched.
No deploy config, migration script or release tooling is in the diff; the after-deploy PATCH is an ops step outside the change.

summary: The local review reported nothing at all, missing even the sub-task the item spelled out by filename (the billing.js 'daily' fallback) plus the double-subscription and comp-revocation consequences of making leoRefreshEnabled superadmin-writable; its triage was mostly right except for treating the crawl-cadence cap as unrelated to external calls.
